# Todo List Application Requirement Analysis Report

## 1. Introduction

The Todo List application provides users with a simple and efficient way to manage their personal tasks. The system supports creating, reading, updating, and deleting individual todo items, ensuring secure authentication and role-based access control.

## 2. Business Model

The application aims to offer a minimalistic task management solution to individual users, emphasizing usability and performance. It targets users seeking simple task tracking without overwhelming features.

## 3. User Actors

### 3.1 Guest
Unauthenticated visitors who can register to become users. Guests cannot create or manage todo items.

### 3.2 User
Registered individuals who can create, read, update, and delete their own todo items securely.

### 3.3 Admin
Administrators with full access rights to manage all users and all todo items.

## 4. Functional Requirements

### 4.1 Todo Item Creation
WHEN a registered user submits a new todo item, THE system SHALL create the item with a unique identifier, title, optional description, creation timestamp, and default status as incomplete.

### 4.2 Todo Item Retrieval
WHEN a registered user requests their todo list, THE system SHALL return all todo items belonging to that user with optional filtering by completion status.

### 4.3 Todo Item Update
WHEN a registered user updates a todo item, THE system SHALL verify ownership and allow updates to title, description, and completion status.

### 4.4 Todo Item Deletion
WHEN a registered user deletes a todo item, THE system SHALL verify ownership and remove the item from persistent storage.

### 4.5 Admin Access
THE admin SHALL be able to perform CRUD operations on any todo item and retrieve lists of todo items for any user.

### 4.6 Authentication
WHEN a guest registers, THE system SHALL validate registration details and create a user account.

WHEN a user logs in, THE system SHALL authenticate credentials and create a secure session.

### 4.7 Session Management
THE system SHALL maintain authenticated user sessions securely until explicit logout or session expiry.

## 5. Business Rules

### 5.1 Ownership
THE system SHALL ensure users access only their own todo items.

### 5.2 Data Validation
WHEN creating or updating todo items, THE system SHALL enforce that the title is non-empty and less than 255 characters, and the description if provided is less than 1000 characters.

### 5.3 Identifiers
THE system SHALL assign unique identifiers to all todo items.

## 6. Error Handling

### 6.1 Authentication Failure
IF login credentials are invalid, THEN THE system SHALL deny access with a clear error message.

### 6.2 Authorization Failure
IF a user attempts unauthorized access, THEN THE system SHALL deny the request and log the event.

### 6.3 Validation Errors
IF data validation fails, THEN THE system SHALL reject the operation and respond with detailed error information.

### 6.4 System Errors
IF unexpected errors occur, THEN THE system SHALL respond with a generic error and log details for diagnosis.

## 7. Performance Requirements

THE system SHALL respond to all CRUD operations within 2 seconds 95% of the time and scale gracefully under concurrent load.

## 8. Security and Compliance

THE system SHALL store passwords securely using industry-standard hashing, sanitize inputs to prevent injections, and protect session data with secure tokens.

## 9. Glossary

- **Todo Item**: A task record with a title, optional description, status, and timestamps.
- **CRUD**: Create, Read, Update, Delete operations.
- **Session**: Authenticated state of a user.

## 10. Appendices

Future plans include notification features, recurring task support, and integrations with external productivity tools.

# Todo List Application Requirements Analysis

## 1. Introduction
This document specifies the business requirements and minimal functional scope for a Todo list application. The aim is to provide a backend system with essential functionality that supports creating, managing, tracking, and deleting todo items for authenticated users while enforcing proper access controls.

## 2. User Actors and Permissions
### Actors
- **Guest**: Unauthenticated user with permission to register an account only.
- **User**: Registered user able to create, read, update, and delete own todo items.
- **Admin**: User with full permissions to manage all todo items and user accounts.

### Permissions Matrix
| Permission                 | Guest | User  | Admin |
|----------------------------|-------|-------|-------|
| Register account           | ✅    | ❌    | ❌    |
| Create todo item           | ❌    | ✅    | ✅    |
| Read own todo items        | ❌    | ✅    | ✅    |
| Update own todo items      | ❌    | ✅    | ✅    |
| Delete own todo items      | ❌    | ✅    | ✅    |
| Manage all todo items      | ❌    | ❌    | ✅    |
| Manage user accounts       | ❌    | ❌    | ✅    |

## 3. Functional Requirements
### 3.1 Todo Item Creation
WHEN a registered User submits a request to create a new todo item, THE system SHALL create the todo item with fields:
- Title (text)
- Description (optional text)
- Due date (optional date)
- Status (default to "pending")

### 3.2 Todo Item Retrieval
WHEN a User requests the list of todo items, THE system SHALL return all todo items owned by that User.

### 3.3 Todo Item Update
WHEN a User requests to update a todo item they own, THE system SHALL update fields including title, description, due date, and status.

### 3.4 Todo Item Deletion
WHEN a User requests to delete a todo item they own, THE system SHALL permanently remove the todo item from the system.

## 4. Authentication and Authorization
- WHEN a user registers, THE system SHALL create a new account with secure password storage.
- WHEN a user logs in with valid credentials, THE system SHALL issue a JWT access token valid for 15 minutes and a refresh token valid for 7 days.
- WHEN a user logs out, THE system SHALL invalidate the active tokens.
- THE system SHALL enforce access control to prevent unauthorized access to todo items.

## 5. Data Model Overview
The system SHALL maintain a Todo entity with fields: ID (UUID), Title, Description, Due Date, Status, Owner User ID (foreign key).

## 6. User Interface Requirements
- THE system SHALL support API endpoints for all CRUD operations on todo items.
- THE system SHALL support user registration and authentication endpoints.

## 7. Business Rules
- All todo items MUST belong to a registered User.
- Users SHALL NOT access or modify todo items owned by others unless they are Admin.
- Title field SHALL NOT be empty when creating or updating a todo item.

## 8. Error Handling
- WHEN an invalid request is received, THE system SHALL respond with appropriate HTTP status codes (e.g., 400, 401, 403).
- WHEN authentication fails, THE system SHALL provide clear error messages.

## 9. Performance Requirements
- THE system SHALL respond to API requests within 500 milliseconds under typical load.

## 10. Security
- THE system SHALL store passwords securely using industry-standard hashing algorithms.
- THE system SHALL support token revocation and refresh mechanisms.

## 11. Glossary
- **Todo item**: A task entity with descriptive fields used to track personal tasks.
- **JWT**: JSON Web Token used for stateless authentication.

## 12. Appendices
Includes references to user actor roles and authentication mechanisms as detailed in supporting documentation.

# Todo List Application Functional Requirements

## 1. Introduction
The todo list application provides users with a minimal yet fully functional system to create, manage, and track their todo items. The system supports registered users and administrators, with features including todo item creation, editing, deletion, status updates, list retrieval with filtering, and user profile management.

## 2. Functional Requirements

### 2.1 Todo Creation and Management
- WHEN a registered user submits a request to create a new todo item, THE todoList system SHALL create the todo item exclusively associated with the user.
- THE todoList system SHALL validate the todo item title and description with the title being a non-empty string up to 255 characters and description optional up to 1000 characters.
- IF the user submits invalid data such as an empty title or title exceeding length limits, THEN THE todoList system SHALL reject the creation request with a clear validation error message.
- THE todoList system SHALL assign a unique identifier and creation timestamp to each new todo item.
- WHEN a registered user submits modifications to their own todo items, THE todoList system SHALL update the items accordingly.
- THE todoList system SHALL reject modifications to todo items not owned by the requesting user.
- THE todoList system SHALL validate all modified fields using the same criteria as for creation.
- WHEN a registered user requests deletion of their own todo item, THE todoList system SHALL remove the item from the user's list.
- THE todoList system SHALL reject deletion requests for todo items not owned by the user.
- WHEN an administrator requests deletion of any todo item, THE todoList system SHALL remove the specified item.

### 2.2 Completion and Status Updates
- WHEN a registered user toggles the completion status of their todo item, THE todoList system SHALL update the status.
- THE todoList system SHALL track completion status using a boolean `isComplete` field.
- WHEN status update succeeds, THE todoList system SHALL update the modified timestamp.

### 2.3 List Retrieval and Filtering
- WHEN a registered user requests their todo list, THE todoList system SHALL return all todo items for that user, ordered by creation time descending.
- THE todoList system SHALL support optional filtering by completion status.
- THE todoList system SHALL paginate results beyond 50 items with default page size 20.
- WHEN a guest attempts to retrieve todo items, THEN THE todoList system SHALL deny access with an unauthorized error.
- WHEN an administrator requests todo items, THE todoList system SHALL allow retrieval of all users' items with filtering and pagination.

### 2.4 User Profile Management
- WHEN a user registers, THE todoList system SHALL create a user account with provided credentials.
- THE system SHALL require email verification before allowing any todo item operations.
- THE todoList system SHALL support login and token-based authentication.
- WHEN a user updates profile details like display name or password, THE system SHALL validate and persist changes.

## 3. Business Rules and Validation Summary
- Todo items belong exclusively to the user who created them.
- Only owners or administrators may modify or delete todo items.
- Titles must be non-empty strings no longer than 255 characters.
- Descriptions are optional with max length 1000 characters.
- Completion status is a boolean and only changeable by owners.
- All timestamps use ISO 8601 format.

## 4. Error Handling Scenarios

### 4.1 Authorization Failures
- IF a user attempts to access or modify a todo item they do not own, THEN THE system SHALL return a 403 Forbidden response with explanation.

### 4.2 Validation Errors
- IF input fails validation, THEN THE system SHALL respond with 400 Bad Request including detailed error report.

### 4.3 Authentication Required
- IF a request requires authentication and the user is unauthenticated, THEN THE system SHALL return 401 Unauthorized error.

## 5. Performance Requirements
- WHEN a user requests their todo list, THE system SHALL respond within 2 seconds under normal load.
- THE system SHALL handle concurrent requests efficiently.

The Todo List Application provides minimal essential functionality to create, manage, and complete todo items for authenticated users. This document specifies business rules, user interactions, authentication, and access control requirements required to implement the backend.

## Functional Requirements

### Todo Item Management
- WHEN a registered user creates a todo item, THE system SHALL assign ownership of the todo item to that user.
- THE user SHALL be able to create, read, update, and delete their own todo items.
- THE system SHALL validate todo item data for correctness before accepting creation or update. Fields such as title and description SHALL meet length and format constraints.
- THE status field of a todo item SHALL accept only "pending", "in-progress", or "completed" values.
- IF a todo item is marked as "completed", THEN the system SHALL prevent edits to title and description.

### User Authentication and Authorization
- WHEN any operation is requested, other than viewing public information, THE system SHALL authenticate the user.
- GUEST users SHALL only have read access to public information and be restricted from creating, updating, or deleting todo items.
- ADMIN users SHALL have full access including the ability to manage all users and todo items.
- OWNERSHIP of todo items MAY NOT be transferred between users.

## User Scenarios
1. **User Registration and Login:** Users register and log in to access personal todo items.
2. **Todo Item Creation:** Users create todo items with title, optional description, status, and optional due date.
3. **Todo Item Update:** Users update their todo items, subject to validation and ownership.
4. **Todo Item Completion:** Users mark todo items as completed, locking title and description fields.
5. **Todo Item Deletion:** Users delete their owned todo items.
6. **Admin Management:** Admins view and manage all todo items and user roles.

## Business Rules

### Ownership Rules
- WHEN a user creates a todo item, THE system SHALL assign ownership to them.
- ONLY owners and admins may edit or delete a todo item.
- OWNERSHIP transfer is disallowed.

### Data Validation
- Titles SHALL be non-empty strings of 1-255 characters.
- Optional descriptions SHALL be strings up to 1000 characters.
- Due dates, if provided, SHALL comply with ISO 8601 format.
- Status values SHALL be restricted to "pending", "in-progress", or "completed".
- WHEN status is "completed", title and description edits are forbidden.

### Access Control
- AUTHENTICATION is mandatory for modification operations.
- GUESTS have read-only, public access.
- ADMINS have unrestricted access.
- Unauthorized access attempts SHALL return an error.

### Auditing and Logging
- All create, update, and delete actions SHALL be logged with user info, timestamp, and todo item ID.
- Logs SHALL be immutable to preserve audit integrity.

## Authentication
- THE system SHALL require user authentication via secure means.
- SESSION management SHALL prevent unauthorized access.
- ROLE-based permissions SHALL enforce access control rules.

## Error Handling
- VALIDATION errors SHALL provide clear messages describing the issue.
- UNAUTHORIZED attempts SHALL respond with appropriate status codes.
- SYSTEM errors SHALL trigger logging and graceful recovery.

## Performance
- SYSTEM SHALL respond to requests within acceptable latency.
- SCALABILITY SHALL allow multiple concurrent users.

## Security
- DATA privacy SHALL be enforced.
- ALL access SHALL be validated.
- INCIDENT response procedures SHALL be defined.

## Glossary
- "Owner": User who created the todo item.
- "Admin": User with elevated privileges.
- "Guest": Unauthenticated user.

This document defines the functional and non-functional requirements for the Todo List application. The goal is to create a minimal yet complete backend system that manages user tasks efficiently and securely.

### 2.1 Todo Item Management
- WHEN a user creates a todo item, THE system SHALL store the item with a title, optional description, creation timestamp, and status (defaulting to pending).
- WHEN a user updates a todo item, THE system SHALL allow modification of title, description, and status.
- WHEN a user deletes a todo item, THE system SHALL remove it from the system permanently.
- WHEN a user requests their todo list, THE system SHALL retrieve all todo items belonging to that user.

### 2.2 Status Values
- The status field SHALL permit only the following values: "pending", "completed", and "archived".
- WHEN a todo item's status changes to "completed", THE system SHALL record the completion timestamp.

### 2.3 Filtering and Sorting
- WHEN a user requests their todo list, THE system SHALL support filtering by status.
- WHEN a user requests their todo list, THE system SHALL support sorting by creation date or completion date.

## 3. Business Rules

### 3.1 Ownership and Access
- WHEN a user accesses todo items, THE system SHALL retrieve only those items created by that user.
- WHEN a user attempts to access or modify todo items they do not own, THE system SHALL deny access.

### 3.2 Data Validation
- WHEN a new todo item is created or updated, THE system SHALL validate that the title is provided and does not exceed 255 characters.
- The description field SHALL be optional but if provided, it SHALL not exceed 1024 characters.
- Status updates SHALL comply with allowed status values.

### 3.3 Auditing
- THE system SHALL record creation, update, and deletion timestamps for each todo item.
- THE system SHALL log user actions related to todo items for audit trails.

## 4. User Authentication and Authorization

### 4.1 User Authentication
- WHEN a user attempts to log in with valid credentials, THE system SHALL authenticate the user and issue a JWT token valid for 30 minutes.
- WHEN a user logs out, THE system SHALL invalidate the JWT token immediately.
- WHEN a user's session expires after 30 minutes of inactivity, THE system SHALL require re-authentication.

### 4.2 User Roles and Permissions
- The system SHALL define at least two user roles: "user" and "admin".
- "user" role SHALL be permitted to manage their own todo items only.
- "admin" role SHALL have permissions to view and manage all users and todo items.

### 4.3 Authorization Checks
- WHEN a user requests access to a resource, THE system SHALL verify the user's role and ownership.
- THE system SHALL deny unauthorized access attempts and log them.

## 5. Error Handling

- WHEN a user attempts to log in with incorrect credentials, THE system SHALL reject the request with an error message within 2 seconds.
- WHEN a user fails 5 consecutive authentication attempts, THE system SHALL lock the account for 30 minutes and notify the user.
- WHEN a user's JWT token is invalid or expired, THE system SHALL deny access and request re-authentication.

### 5.2 Authorization Failures
- WHEN a user attempts unauthorized actions, THE system SHALL deny the operation and log the incident.

### 5.3 Input Validation Errors
- WHEN requests contain missing required fields or invalid formats, THE system SHALL reject the request with descriptive error messages.
- WHEN a todo title exceeds 255 characters or description exceeds 1024 characters, THE system SHALL reject the request.
- WHEN status values are invalid, THE system SHALL reject the update request.

### 5.4 System Errors
- In case of unexpected internal errors, THE system SHALL respond with a generic error message and log details.
- IF the database is unavailable, THE system SHALL retry connection up to three times before failing.

## 6. Performance Requirements

- The system SHALL respond to all user requests within 2 seconds under normal load.
- The system SHALL support at least 100 concurrent users.

## 7. Security and Compliance

- THE system SHALL store passwords securely using salted hashing.
- THE system SHALL use HTTPS for all client-server communications.
- THE system SHALL comply with applicable data protection regulations.

## 8. Glossary

- "Todo Item": A task entered by a user to be completed.
- "JWT Token": JSON Web Token used for authentication.
- "User Roles": Defined roles with specific permissions.
- "EARS Format": Easy Approach to Requirements Syntax, a formal method for writing requirements.

- References to security standards and libraries.
- List of future enhancements such as multi-user collaboration and reminders.

This document specifies the business requirements for a minimal Todo List application. The purpose is to clearly define the features, user roles, business rules, and security considerations necessary to build a functional and secure Todo List backend.

## 3. User Actors

- **User**: Authenticated user who can manage their own todo items.

- WHEN a user is authenticated, THE system SHALL allow the user to read the list of their own todo items.

### 4.2 Todo Item Attributes

# Todo List Application Requirements Analysis Report

## 1. Introduction

The Todo List application provides a minimal yet functional digital tool allowing users to effectively manage their tasks. This specification outlines the business requirements, intended to guide backend development of a secure, reliable, and maintainable service based on clear, natural language descriptions.

## 2. Business Model

The Todo List service exists to fulfill the widespread demand for a simple, easy-to-use personal task management tool. It targets users seeking efficiency without complicated features. Although the initial scope is basic and free, revenue streams may emerge from premium features or subscriptions in future expansions.

Organic growth via user referral and simple, reliable functionality form the core of the growth strategy. Success will be measured primarily by active user counts, engagement metrics such as tasks created and completed, and consistent system uptime and response times.

## 3. User Actors

Three primary user roles define the system's interaction boundaries:

- **Guest**: Can view public resources and register accounts but cannot manage todos.
- **User**: Registered individuals able to create, view, update, and delete their own todo items.
- **Admin**: System administrators with full control over all users and todo items.

Permissions are finely controlled; guests have minimal access, users can manage only their data, and admins have comprehensive management rights.

## 4. Functional Requirements

- WHEN a registered user submits a new todo item, THE system SHALL create and persist the todo with a unique identifier.
- WHEN a registered user requests their todo list, THE system SHALL retrieve all todo items owned by that user.
- WHEN a registered user updates an existing todo, THE system SHALL verify ownership before applying changes.
- WHEN a registered user deletes a todo, THE system SHALL verify ownership before removing it permanently.
- THE system SHALL support the following todo attributes: title (mandatory text), description (optional text), creation timestamp, optional due date, and completion status (boolean).
- WHEN a user marks a todo as complete, THE system SHALL update the completion status accordingly.

## 5. Business Rules

- THE system SHALL restrict todo access and modification strictly to the owning user.
- THE system SHALL enforce non-empty titles on all todos.
- THE system SHALL reject any todo creation or update requests with due dates set in the past.
- THE system SHALL automatically assign the creation timestamp at the moment of todo creation.

## 6. Error Handling

- IF a guest attempts to create, update, or delete a todo, THEN THE system SHALL respond with an authorization error.
- IF a user attempts to access or modify a todo not owned by them, THEN THE system SHALL deny the request with an appropriate error message.
- IF validation fails due to missing title or invalid due date, THEN THE system SHALL return an informative error identifying the problematic inputs.
- IF any unexpected system error occurs, THEN THE system SHALL return a generic error message to the user and log the incident internally for review.

## 7. Performance Requirements

- THE system SHALL respond to all todo operations (creation, reading, updating, deletion) within 2 seconds under normal operating conditions.
- THE system SHALL maintain data consistency and support concurrent operations from multiple users without errors or race conditions.

## 8. Diagrams

```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Start: User Logged In"] --> B["Create New Todo"]
  B --> C["Validate Input"]
  C --> D{"Valid Input?"}
  D -->|"Yes"| E["Store Todo"]
  D -->|"No"| F["Return Validation Error"]
  E --> G["Confirm Creation"]
  G --> H["End"]
  F --> H

    I["Retrieve Todos"] --> J["Update Todo"]
    J --> K["Delete Todo"]
  end

  A --> I
  K --> H
```

## 9. Future Considerations

Future development may include features such as categorizing and tagging todos, user notifications and reminders, collaborative todo management, and mobile as well as offline access capabilities.

ITodoListGuestSession.description:
Represents a session record for a guest visitor of the Todo List application.

This schema captures detailed information including the unique identifier, associated guest, IP address, connection URLs, and lifecycle timestamps relevant to the session's creation and expiration.

It provides essential context for tracking anonymous sessions used for visit management and interaction tracking within the application.

id.description: Unique identifier of the guest session.

todo_list_guest_id.description: Foreign key referencing the owning todo list guest.

ip.description: IP address from which the session originated.

href.description: Connection URL where the session was established.

referrer.description: Referrer URL indicating the source of the session visit.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the session expires or null if the session is active.

ITodoListGuestSession.ICreate.description:
Request payload schema for creating a new guest session associated with a specific todo list guest.

Includes session details such as the originating IP address, connection URL, referrer URL, creation timestamp, and optional expiration timestamp. This facilitates anonymous session tracking for guests.

ip.description: IP address from which the session originates.

href.description: Connection URL for establishing the session.

referrer.description: Referrer URL indicating the navigation source for the session.

created_at.description: Timestamp marking the creation time of the session.

expired_at.description: Expiration timestamp for the session; may be null if the session is ongoing.

ITodoListGuestSession.IUpdate.description:
Request object for updating an existing guest session associated with a specific todoListGuest.

Allows modification of the IP address, connection URL, referrer URL, session creation and expiration timestamps.

System-managed fields like the session identifiers are excluded because they are path parameters or managed internally.

Authorization is required, and the updating actor is the authenticated user responsible for this session modification.

This DTO excludes authenticated user identity fields which are derived from JWT/token context rather than the request body.

ip.description: IP address of the session connection. This field records the visitor's IP address for session tracking and security purposes.

href.description: Connection URL for the session. This field stores the URL where the session was initiated or currently active.

referrer.description: Referrer URL for the session indicating the previous page URL before this session activity.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the session was created. This reflects the session start time.

expired_at.description: Session expiration time. Nullable timestamp which indicates when the session is set to expire. If null, session is currently active.

ITodoListTodoListUser.IRequest.description: Parameters for searching and filtering users in the Todo List application, including pagination and advanced criteria.

page.description: Page number for pagination, starting at 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of users to return per page.

search.description: Search keyword to filter users by their email or other attributes.

created_from.description: Filter users created at or after this date and time.

created_to.description: Filter users created at or before this date and time.

is_active.description: Filter to select active or inactive users.

ITodoListTodoListUser.description:
Represents a registered user in the Todo List application. Contains essential user information for authentication and profile management while excluding sensitive data such as password hashes.

Used in responses to provide user details without exposing security-sensitive fields.

id.description: Unique UUID identifier of the user.

email.description: Email address of the user used for login and communication. Must be unique.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the user was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the user information was last updated.

ITodoListTodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
Data structure for updating attributes of a registered Todo List user. All fields are optional and only specified fields will be updated.

Immutable fields like `id` are excluded. Sensitive fields like passwords are managed via dedicated operations and are not part of this update schema.

email.description: Updated email address of the user.

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description: Parameters for searching and listing user sessions associated with a specific Todo List user, supporting filtering, sorting, and pagination.

page.description: Page number for paginated results, starting from 1.

limit.description: Number of sessions to return per page.

search.description: Search keyword to filter sessions by related fields such as IP or referrer URL.

sortBy.description: Field name to sort the list by.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todoListUserSession record.

todo_list_user_id.description: Unique identifier of the owning todoListUser.

ip.description: IP address of the session connection.

expired_at.description: Session expiration time, null if session is currently active.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
Session record representing an authenticated session of a registered Todo List user.

This entity tracks connection details such as IP, access path, and referrer along with session lifecycle timestamps.

Each session is owned by a specific user identified by todo_list_user_id, linking to the todo_list_users table.

The expired_at property is nullable to signify an active or expired session.

Do NOT include sensitive authentication tokens in this schema.

ITodoListUserSession.ICreate.description:
Schema for creating a new authenticated session record linked to a registered Todo List user.

This schema includes connection metadata fields such as IP address, page URL, and referrer for comprehensive session tracking.
The session expiration time is optional and may be null if the session is active.

The user ID is removed from request body because it comes from authenticated JWT and must not be accepted from client input.

All other properties remain intact.

This model corresponds to the todo_list_user_sessions table in Prisma.

ip.description: IP address of the session connection.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) for this session.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) for this session.

expired_at.description: Session expiration time in ISO 8601 format. If null, the session is currently active.

page.description: Page number for paginated query of todo list administrators. Defaults to 1 if omitted.

limit.description: Maximum number of items per page for pagination, default 20.

search_email.description: Filter administrators by email address containing the given string.

status.description: Filter administrators by account status (active, inactive, suspended).

created_at_from.description: Filter administrators created at or after this date and time (inclusive). Format is ISO 8601.

created_at_to.description: Filter administrators created at or before this date and time (inclusive). Format is ISO 8601.

updated_at_from.description: Filter administrators updated at or after this date and time (inclusive). Format is ISO 8601.

updated_at_to.description: Filter administrators updated at or before this date and time (inclusive). Format is ISO 8601.

ITodoListAdmin.IRequest.description: Parameters for searching and paginating Todo List administrator accounts. Includes filtering by email, account status, and creation/update timestamps.

ITodoListAdmin.description:
Represents administrators of the Todo List application who possess full system privileges.

This entity manages admin authentication details including a unique identifier, email, and lifecycle timestamps. It is the foundation for administrative control and access management.

This schema is used to represent Todo List administrators in various API responses.

**Note: password_hash field removed to prevent exposing hashed passwords.**

id.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the Todo List administrator.

email.description: Admin email address for authentication and communication.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the admin account was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the admin account was last updated.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the admin account was soft deleted, if applicable; null indicates the account is active.

ITodoListAdminSession.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for filtering, sorting, and paginating Todo List administrator session records.

Supports filtering by session creation time and session expiration status. Paging through session records is supported via standard pagination fields.

This request schema is designed to be used with the admin sessions listing endpoint to facilitate session management and monitoring.

page.description: Page number for paginated results, starting from 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of records per page to return.

sort_by.description: Field name to sort the results by, e.g., 'created_at'.

expired.description: Filter sessions based on expiration status. `true` filters for expired sessions; `false` for active sessions.

ITodoListAdminSession.description:
Represents a session record for an administrator of the Todo List application.

Each session associates with a specific admin user, recording connection metadata such as IP address, connection URL, and referrer URL. It tracks session inception and optional expiration timestamps to support session lifecycle management.

This schema excludes any sensitive authentication credentials and only exposes session metadata for management and auditing purposes.

id.description: Unique identifier of the admin session record.

todoListAdminId.description: The unique identifier of the admin who owns this session.

ip.description: IP address from which the admin connected for the session.

href.description: Connection URL associated with the admin session.

referrer.description: Referrer URL from which the admin session originated.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the session expires. Null if the session is currently active and has no expiration time.

ITodoListAdminSession.ICreate.description:
Request payload schema to create a new Todo List administrator session.

This schema requires connection context attributes, including IP address, connection URL, referrer URL, and optional session expiration time.

The admin identifier is extracted from the authorization context and thus excluded from the request body to prevent spoofing and ensure security.

href.description: Current page URL where the session was created.

referrer.description: Referrer URL that led to the session creation page.

expired_at.description: Optional expiration datetime of the session. Null indicates no expiration time set.

ITodoListAdminSession.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating an admin session record in the Todo List application.

Allows modification of connection information and session expiration time.

Actor identity is inferred from authentication context; no actor ID included.

All properties are optional to permit partial updates.

ip.description: IP address of the session connection.

href.description: Connection URL where the session was established.

referrer.description: Referrer URL from where the session was initiated.

expired_at.description: Expiration timestamp of the session; null if session is currently active.

ITodoListTodo.IRequest.description:
Search filter and pagination request body for querying Todo List todo items.

Allows clients to specify various filters such as completion status, keyword search, and pagination controls for efficient retrieval of user's todo items.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Defaults to first page if omitted.

limit.description: Maximum number of items per page. Helps control payload size and response time.

search.description: Keyword query to search todo item titles and descriptions.

is_complete.description: Flag to filter todo items by their completion status. True for completed items, false otherwise.

ITodoListTodo.description:
Represents an individual task item managed by a registered user within the Todo List application.

Each todo item includes a unique identifier, ownership reference to a user, and metadata such as title, description, completion status, and standard timestamps for creation, updates, and soft deletion.

Ownership ensures only the associated user can manipulate their todos. Soft deletion preserves historical data and enables reversible removal.

Used as the main response type for todo item retrieval operations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo item.

todoListUserId.description: Unique identifier of the user that owns this todo item.

title.description: Title of the todo item, required and limited to a reasonable length for usability.

description.description: Optional detailed description providing additional context for the todo item.

isComplete.description: Indicates whether the todo item has been marked as completed.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the todo item was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the todo item was last updated.

deletedAt.description: Timestamp indicating soft deletion status; null if not deleted.

title.description: Title of the todo item, required and limited to a reasonable length for usability.

oneOf.description: Optional detailed description of the todo item providing additional context and information.

description.description: Optional detailed description of the todo item providing additional context and information.

isComplete.description: Flag indicating whether the todo item is marked as completed.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for todo list items representing individual tasks managed by registered users.

This schema requires the todo item's title and completion status to create a new task.
The description field is optional and provides additional context when specified.
The owner user ID and timestamps are handled by the system and are excluded to enforce security and integrity.

Used as the request body when creating new todo items through the API.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description:
Payload to update an existing todo item owned by the user.

Allows modification of title, description, and completion status. Ownership and soft deletion status are managed by the system and cannot be changed here.

This interface excludes immutable fields such as IDs and timestamps. All properties are optional to allow partial updates.

Security fixes applied: removed authentication context fields, system-managed timestamps, and path parameters from request body.

title.description: Updated title of the todo item. Must be a non-empty string.

description.description: Updated optional detailed description for the todo item. Null to clear.

isComplete.description: Updated completion status flag for the todo item.

id.description: Unique identifier of the todo list system configuration

value.description: Configuration value associated with the key

ITodoListGuest.ISummary.description:
Summary information of a guest visitor to the Todo List application.

Represents an unregistered user visiting the platform with minimal tracking information including unique ID and IP address. Contains temporal metadata for creation and last update events.

expired_at.description: Session expiration time, null if session is currently active.

ITodoListGuestSession.ISummary.description:
Summary information for a guest visitor's session in the Todo List application.

Tracks session lifecycle and connection context for unregistered guest users, including references to the owning guest, connection details, and timestamps for creation and expiration.

ITodoListTodoListUser.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a registered user in the Todo List application.

Provides the minimal essential details to identify and display a user within the system without exposing sensitive data.

Includes only publicly visible fields necessary for user references and listings.

email.description: Email address of the user used for authentication and communication.

ITodoListUserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an authenticated user session in the Todo List application.

Provides the essential details to identify an active user session including connection metadata.

Used for listing sessions without exposing sensitive information such as session tokens.

id.description: Unique identifier of the user session.

todo_list_user_id.description: Unique identifier referencing the user who owns this session.

ip.description: IP address from which the session was established.

href.description: Connection URL where the session was initiated.

referrer.description: Referrer URL indicating the previous page leading to the session connection.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the user session was created.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the session expires. Null if the session is currently active.

ITodoListAdmin.ISummary.description:
Summary information of a Todo List Administrator.

Represents a lightweight view of an administrator including unique identifier, email, and timestamps indicating the account lifecycle. Used for list views and embedded references within the Todo List system.

id.description: Unique UUID identifier for the Todo List Administrator.

email.description: Email address of the administrator used for authentication and notification.

created_at.description: Timestamp marking when the administrator account was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp marking when the administrator account was last updated.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp marking when the administrator account was soft-deleted, or null if the account is active.

ITodoListAdminSession.ISummary.description:
Summary information of a Todo List Administrator's session.

Provides essential details about an administrator session including the unique session identifier, reference to the owning administrator, connection metadata, and timestamps marking session lifecycle events.

id.description: Unique UUID identifier for the admin session.

todo_list_admin_id.description: UUID of the administrator owning this session.

ip.description: IP address from which the session was established.

href.description: Connection URL indicating where the session was initiated.

referrer.description: Referrer URL indicating the previous page leading to the session.

created_at.description: Timestamp marking when the session was created.

expired_at.description: Timestamp marking when the session expired, or null if the session is active.

id.description: Unique identifier of the todo item.

title.description: Title of the todo item, summarizing the task to be done.

is_complete.description: Completion status flag of the todo item, indicating if the task is done.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the todo item was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the todo item was last updated.

ITodoListTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a Todo List item.

Provides essential details for list views including task identity, title, completion status, and timestamps.

This schema excludes detailed description and deletion info, optimized for performance and minimal data transfer.

ITodoListTodoListUser.ICreate.description:
User registration data for the todo_list_users table.

Includes essential details to register a new user account with secure password hashing and timestamps for auditing.

This schema ensures clients provide necessary information for user creation while keeping sensitive details protected.

SECURED VERSION: Removed hashed password and system-managed timestamp fields from input.

email.description: The unique email address of the user. This field is used as the primary identifier for authentication and communication.

name.description: The display name for the user account.

id.description: Unique UUID identifier of the authorized user in the todo_list_users table.

ITodoListTodoListUser.IAuthorized.description: Response schema representing an authorized user with a unique ID and a JWT token indicating successful authentication and authorization.

ITodoListTodoListUser.ILogin.description:
Login credentials for authenticating a registered user in the todo_list_users table.

Includes email and password in plain text along with session connection metadata.

The 'email' field replaces 'email_or_username' for direct Prisma property mapping.

Session connection details include optional IP address, mandatory current page URL (href), and mandatory referrer URL.

Used by the authentication system to validate login attempts and initiate user sessions securely.

email.description: Email address of the user attempting to login; used as primary identifier for authentication.

password.description: User plaintext password for verification during login.

ip.description: Client IP address for session tracking (optional).

href.description: Current page URL where the login is initiated (mandatory).

refreshToken.description: The refresh token issued to the user for renewing the access token. This token must be valid, unexpired, and linked to a user in the todo_list_users table to allow refreshing the JWT access token.

ITodoListTodoListUser.IRefresh.description: Request schema for refreshing JWT access tokens by submitting a valid refresh token linked to a registered user in the todo_list_users database. This operation extends the authenticated session securely using the refresh token mechanism.

currentPassword.description: Current password of the user. Used for verifying user identity before applying the password change.

newPassword.description: The new password to be securely stored after hashing. Must meet the system's password policy requirements.

ITodoListTodoListUser.IVerifyEmail.description:
Request body schema for verifying a registered user's email address.

This schema contains the fields necessary to confirm ownership of the email address via verification token and user identification. It enables secure confirmation workflows ensuring only the legitimate user can verify their email.

This operation supports security mechanisms such as token expiration and anti-replay protection.

Mapped directly to the todo_list_users domain.

email.description: Email address of the user to verify. Must match the registered user's email.

verification_token.description: Unique token sent to the user's email for verification purposes. Used to validate ownership and confirm email address authenticity.

ITodoListTodoListUser.IEnableTwoFactor.description:
Request body schema for enabling two-factor authentication (2FA) for a registered user.

This schema includes the necessary fields to initiate 2FA setup, such as the authentication token or verification code.

It facilitates enhanced account security by requiring an additional verification step beyond the password.

Applicable only if 2FA is supported in the todo_list_users schema.

two_factor_token.description: Token or code used to enable and activate two-factor authentication. Validated to ensure authenticity and prevent unauthorized activations.

ITodoListGuest.description:
Represents a guest user in the Todo List application who visits without registration. This entity captures essential visitor information such as their IP address and timestamps for record creation and updates.

Guests are anonymous users with limited capabilities compared to registered users. Their information is used for tracking, session management, and analytics within the app.

Fields included reflect direct columns from the corresponding Prisma model, excluding any sensitive or system-managed fields not meant for client interaction.

id.description: Unique identifier for the guest user. Generated automatically upon creation.

visitor_ip.description: IP address of the guest visitor for tracking purposes.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this guest record was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this guest record was last updated.

ITodoListGuest.ICreate.description:
Data required to create a new guest user in the Todo List application.

Only the visitor's IP address is needed since the unique identifier and timestamps are managed by the system automatically. This minimal data set allows for guest session initiation and tracking.

The creation DTO excludes system-managed fields and identity keys, following secure API design principles.

visitor_ip.description: IP address of the guest visitor required for creation.

ITodoListGuest.IUpdate.description: DTO for updating a Todo List guest record, allowing modification of mutable guest information such as visitor IP. System and ownership fields including timestamps are excluded for security reasons.

visitor_ip.description: IP address of the guest visitor for tracking purposes. Updating this allows modification of the IP address associated with the guest.

ip.description: IP address of the session connection.

expired_at.description: Session expiration time, null if session is currently active.

ITodoListUserSession.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for todoListUserSession, allowing modification of connection details and expiration time.

Properties are optional and only those provided will be updated.

Sensitive fields like user_id and created_at are not modifiable via this DTO.

ITodoListAdmin.IUpdate.description:
Data structure for updating an existing Todo List administrator's information.

Allows modification of mutable fields such as email. Password hashing is managed internally, so password_hash is removed from request DTO.

System timestamps are managed server-side and accept null.

Admin ID cannot be changed through this update DTO.

email.description: Admin email address for authentication and communication.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the admin account was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the admin account was last updated.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the admin account was soft deleted, if applicable; null indicates the account is active.
